name: Learn basic improv comedy
blurb: The principles — yes-and, make your partner look good, play the top of your intelligence — improve ordinary conversation and meetings as much as they improve performance.
gear: A class or a group; improv genuinely cannot be learned alone
steps: Learn “yes, and”: accept the reality your partner offers and add to it, rather than blocking or questioning it.
Learn to make offers that are specific. “I brought the ashes” gives your partner something; “hi” gives them nothing.
Learn to listen properly — improv fails when you plan your next line instead of hearing the current one.
Practise character work through physicality and voice rather than accents and jokes.
Learn to find the game of a scene: the first unusual thing, then heighten it.
Join a drop-in class. Six weeks of a beginner course covers all of this with people to practise on.
tips: Trying to be funny is what makes improv unfunny. Commit to the reality and the comedy follows.
Denying your partner’s offer is the cardinal sin and instantly kills a scene.
proof: You play a three-minute scene that builds coherently and gets genuine laughs, without going for jokes.
